cases.evIsTheAverageValue:
EV is the average value of a drop after the fee, the sum over rarities of chance × average price of the skins of that rarity.
Valve's odds are blue 79.92%, purple 15.98%, pink 3.20%, red 0.64% and knife/gloves 0.26%. StatTrak™ 10%.
Case contents and float ranges come from the game files (the ByMykel/CSGO-API set). The wear is worked out from the skin's float range (e.g. a Doppler drops as FN about 96% of the time).
Loss per opening is cost − EV, what you lose on average per opening (in the long run, a single drop can be worth much more or less). The table is sorted from the smallest loss.
Capsules need no key, so the cost is the capsule price. Sticker rarities are High Grade (normal), Remarkable (holo / glitter / embroidered), Exotic (foil / holo) and Extraordinary (gold), with the same odds as cases (79.92 / 15.98 / 3.20 / 0.64) spread over the rarities the capsule has (that's how capsule data sites do it, Valve doesn't publish separate odds). Contents come from the game files (ByMykel), prices from the Steam market.
Prices are the lowest listing on the Steam market (single expensive drops often sell a bit cheaper in practice, so EV tends to be slightly too high). Cost is case + key. For a case marked "I have it" (ticked automatically when it's in your inventory, once the Inventory tab has loaded) the cost is the key plus what selling that case would bring you (after the fee). "Chance to break even" is how often a drop is worth as much as the opening costs.
cases.theAverageResultOfOne: The average result of one opening, EV − cost, so what an opening costs you on average. Smallest loss first.

flip.downloadsFromTheSteamMarket: Downloads the order book and the full price history of the items now on the list (scanner, watchlist or the analysed item) from the Steam market and saves them to a file, to check whether they really pay off. When the list is empty, it takes a fixed sample of about 100 popular items. Nothing is bought or listed.
flip.picksAFewHundredRandom: Picks a few hundred random items from the most popular ones on the Steam market (evenly from every kind and price range) and saves their price history and order book to a file, to test Flipster's algorithms on a wider market. Nothing is bought or listed.
flip.itemNameInEnglishOr: Item (name in English or Polish, or a market link)
flip.onlyItemsWithTheFlip: Only items with the “Flip possible” verdict stay on the list. Untick it to also see the risky ones (profit smaller than the typical weekly price swing).
flip.tickedTheScannerReusesWhat: When ticked, the scanner reuses what it checked recently, such as rejected items (12 h when the order book alone left no room for a flip, 3 h after a full check), hits and “risky” ones (30 min), and lists and order books (a few minutes). Untick it to download everything from Steam again for this scan.
flip.removesTheResultsOfThe: Removes the results of the previous scan from the list (also the ones kept across a page reload). Watched and hidden items stay.
flip.theScannerTakesTheMost:
The scanner takes the most popular items of the category and price range from the Steam market, and for each of them the order book and the full price history.
Long term. Shows how holding the item paid off in the past, after the fee, meaning how many winters (bought at the end of November, sold half a year later) ended in profit, the result after one and after two years, the price against the yearly average and the change over the last month. A “candidate” is a case older than 4 years, from 1 zł, whose price didn't fall more than 10% in 30 days and which sells ≥ 20 units a day. The case's own winter record is shown but isn't used, because in the research it didn't separate better cases from worse ones, while age did. For other items, at least 3 winters of data and a profit in ≥ 70% of them.
Quick flip. Buy with an order one cent above the orders actually in the order book, sell at the price items actually sell for, minus the fee. A bought item can only be listed after 7 days, so next to it you see the typical weekly price swing and whether anyone sold that cheap lately. In this mode the scanner keeps going down the list, from the most popular items, until it finds as many “Flip possible” items as you set in “How many to find”, the list runs out or you click Stop. An empty “How many to find” means no limit, it searches until Stop. With “profitable only” just the hits stay on the list, untick it to also see the “risky” ones.
Where these rules come from. Research on 108 items with up to 13 years of history (15.11.2026). Flips and buying dips didn't beat the fee, while holding old cases bought in winter made money. New items usually lose a lot of value. This is history, not a guarantee.
